sources.entry: numba - A NumPy-aware JIT compiler for Python, using LLVM.

summary.one_liner: Numba is an open-source, NumPy-aware just-in-time compiler that uses LLVM to turn numerically focused Python functions into machine code.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Numba as an optimizing compiler for Python, sponsored by Anaconda, Inc., that uses the LLVM compiler project to generate machine code from Python syntax. It says Numba can compile a large subset of numerically focused Python, including many NumPy functions. It also states support for automatic parallelization of loops, generation of GPU-accelerated code, and creation of ufuncs and C callbacks. The README itself is mostly a landing page: installation, demo and contact sections point to external pages and do not include commands or details in the text provided.
use_cases: speed up numerical loops in Python
how_to_run: See the installation instructions on the Numba homepage or documentation (the README links out and gives no commands).
notable: JIT compiles numerical Python to machine code via LLVM
can create ufuncs and C callbacks
caveats: Supports only a large subset of Python, focused on numerical code
README gives no install commands; points to external documentation
Some features (GPU code) are named but not detailed in the README
